title: Push system
description: Cashier and restaurant management system in Arabic for Windows.
markdown:
**An Arabic-language point-of-sale and restaurant management system for Windows.**

Push brings order management, products, inventory, customers, reporting, and receipt printing together in a desktop application with a dark, right-to-left interface.

**Version:** 1.3.5 · **Technology:** C# / Windows Forms / .NET Framework 4.8 / SQLite

## Features

- Product catalog that adapts to the window size, with barcode search.
- Order view with columns for item name, quantity, price, and total, plus discounts and notes.
- Support for takeaway, delivery, table service, and corporate orders.
- Product, customer, inventory, and expense management, plus sales reporting.
- Sign-in before opening the register, with separate manager and staff accounts.
- Arabic receipt printing and reprinting for previous orders.
- Data backup and recovery.
- Custom restaurant name, phone numbers, address, receipt footer, and restaurant image.
- The image selected during installation appears in the application, on receipts, and as the executable icon.
- The installer names the executable and shortcut after the restaurant, including support for Arabic names.
- Permanent offline activation for one device using a signed license file.

## Management and optional features — 1.3.5

The **Management** button next to Settings is available only to managers. It includes:

- **Purchases and suppliers:** Add suppliers, ingredients, and units of measure. Record deliveries for individual ingredients, track amounts paid and outstanding, settle supplier balances, and view account statements. Purchases are tracked separately from register shift expenses.
- **Recipes and item costing:** Specify the quantity of each ingredient for one unit of an item. Calculate costs using the weighted average purchase price and view the selling margin before expenses and discounts. Recipes apply to the base item. Ingredient quantities for variants and add-ons are not tracked separately.

Ingredient stock is deducted when a sale is completed. Held orders do not reduce stock. Editing an order restores the quantities it previously consumed before calculating its new stock usage. Use the same unit for deliveries and recipes, as kilograms and grams are not converted automatically. Selling more than the available stock can produce a negative balance, which helps identify unrecorded deliveries.

Under **Settings → Operations → Optional features**, each option can be enabled separately:

| Option | Behavior when enabled |
| --- | --- |
| Cash drawer | Adds a register button and opens the drawer automatically for cash payments via the connected ESC/POS printer |
| Kitchen display | Opens a separate window that refreshes every two seconds and shows New, Preparing, and Ready statuses |
| Kitchen printer | Sends a kitchen copy to the selected printer in addition to printing the customer receipt when a sale is completed |

These options are off by default. The corresponding register buttons appear only when their features are enabled. The kitchen display runs on the same computer and can be moved to a second screen. This version has no standalone network kitchen client. Kitchen orders are collected from the time the feature is enabled. Older orders are not imported automatically. The drawer uses a standard ESC/POS pulse on port 0, and actual operation depends on the hardware and its connections.

## User permissions

| Action | Manager | Staff |
| --- | :---: | :---: |
| Use the register and complete sales | ✓ | ✓ |
| View and reprint previous orders | ✓ | ✓ |
| Edit a completed order | — | — |
| Open Settings | ✓ | — |

Only managers can access Settings. No user can edit a completed order. Held orders can still be resumed, and receipts can be reprinted.

## Client installation

1. Run `PushPOS-Setup.exe`.
2. Enter the restaurant name and details, and optionally select a restaurant image.
3. Send the device code shown on the activation screen to meshziadessam@gmail.com to request a `.lic` file.
4. Import the license file, then create the manager account and add staff accounts from Settings.
5. Select a printer in Settings and test receipt printing before going live.

The database is created automatically. The client does not need a Python project or a prepared database. Data is stored in `%LOCALAPPDATA%\PushPOS` and is retained after uninstalling.

The full installer bundles the .NET Framework 4.8 installer. The smaller installer requires .NET Framework 4.8 to be installed beforehand. Changing the restaurant image in Settings updates the interface and receipt. The executable icon is embedded during installation.

## Building the project

Run these commands from the folder containing `RestaurantPos.sln` and `build.ps1`.

### Requirements

- Windows and PowerShell.
- A .NET SDK capable of building .NET Framework 4.8 projects. This project was built using SDK 10.
- Access to NuGet to restore packages on the first build.
- Inno Setup **6.4.3** to build the installer.

Build the application, icon customization utility, and tests:

```powershell
./build.ps1
```

The executable is written to:

```text
src/RestaurantPos/bin/Release/net48/RestaurantPos.exe
```

The internal project name is `RestaurantPos`, while users see **Push**. The installer customizes the executable filename using the restaurant name.

### Building the installer

To create the smaller installer:

```powershell
./build.ps1 -InnoCompiler 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe'
```

To create the full installer, place the original Microsoft installer `ndp48-x86-x64-allos-enu.exe` in `.tools/` and run:

```powershell
./build.ps1 -InnoCompiler 'C:\Program Files (x86)\Inno Setup 6\ISCC.exe' -BundleFramework
```

The build script verifies Microsoft's signature on the Framework installer. You can pass a different local path to `ISCC.exe`. The tools in `.tools/` are excluded from Git and must be supplied when building from a cloned repository.

The output files are in `artifacts/`:

| File | Purpose |
| --- | --- |
| `PushPOS-Setup.exe` | Full client installer |
| `PushPOS-Setup-Small.exe` | Client installer without .NET Framework |

The optional `tools/package_release.py` script packages source and vendor tool archives and computes SHA-256 hashes for the outputs. It requires Python 3. The POS application itself has no Python dependency.

## Testing

After building, run the operational and UI checks:

```powershell
./tests/OperationalChecks/bin/Release/net48/OperationalChecks.exe ./qa-output
```

Run the performance checks:

```powershell
./tests/PerformanceChecks/bin/Release/net48/PerformanceChecks.exe ./performance-output
```

The tests use separate sample data. The last verification after cleaning the project recorded **242 passing operational and release checks** covering sales, inventory, permissions, reports, backup and recovery, and the UI. Physical receipt printing is checked on the client's printer as part of handover.

## Project structure

```text
.
├── src/RestaurantPos/            # Application, database, printing, and activation
├── installer/                   # Inno Setup configuration

├── tests/                       # Operational and performance checks
├── tools/                       # Executable icon customization and release packaging
├── build.ps1                    # Application build and installer packaging
├── RestaurantPos.sln
├── SELLER-GUIDE.md
├── USER-GUIDE.txt
└── THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt
```

## Licensing and GitHub files

The source includes only the **public key** used to verify RSA-4096 / SHA-256 licenses. The private issuing key stays outside the repository. Keep the same key pair across updates so existing client licenses remain valid.

The `.gitignore` file excludes build outputs, databases, activation files, and private keys. Keep `issuer-private.xml`, `.lic` files, customer data, and vendor tool archives out of public repositories. Use a private repository for the commercial source and distribute only the installer to clients. The client installer can be attached to GitHub Releases when needed.

Offline activation rejects licenses issued for another device. It has no remote revocation feature and cannot fully prevent application tampering. License file signing is separate from Windows publisher signing. The current executables do not carry a commercial Authenticode certificate.

See the [Seller Guide](SELLER-GUIDE.md), [User Guide](USER-GUIDE.txt), and [Third-Party Notices](THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES.txt). The repository does not grant an open-source license. Licenses for third-party components are documented in the notices file.

### Discount limit — 1.3.5

Invoice and item discounts combined cannot exceed 30% of the pre-discount invoice total, including add-ons and applicable delivery fees. The cap is rounded down to the nearest piastre so the discount stays within the limit. The discount input shows the available amount. The system checks it again when saving, paying, holding an order, or editing an order after quantities change. Historical invoices remain available to view and reprint.

### HEX button colors — 1.3.5

Under **Settings → Operations → HEX button colors**, change the colors of primary, save and confirm, delete and cancel, and standard buttons for both dark and light modes. Enter a value such as `#3366CC` or `3366CC`. You can preview changes and restore the defaults. Select **Save colors** to apply them. Text automatically switches between white and black based on background contrast. Previewing or canceling does not change saved colors. Settings are retained after a restart and included in backups.

### Completed order editing removed — 1.3.5

The edit button was removed for all roles, and edits to completed orders can no longer be loaded or saved. Held orders can still be resumed, merged, or canceled before completion. Managers and staff can still reprint receipts. Updating the application leaves historical invoices unchanged.
